title: A screen reader hears only 'Edit' or 'Open' on product and app member cards, not the price, stock or orders
what: On Shop products, the top of each card (picture, name, price, stock, Hidden) is one button that a screen reader names only 'Edit <product>'. On Joined in the app, each member card is one button named only 'Open <name>'. The given name replaces everything inside, so a blind owner never hears the price, how many are left, that a product is hidden, or a member's orders and money paid.
expected: The card's button name, or text next to it, includes the facts shown on the card (price, stock, hidden; orders and paid), so a screen reader user gets the same facts as a sighted one.
who: owners and desk staff who use a screen reader
how_often: every time the product list or app members list is read aloud
fix_line: Let the card read out its own words, or add the price, stock and order facts to its spoken name

title: Three product card buttons have a spoken name that does not match the words on them
what: The buttons read '+10 stock', 'Hide from app' and 'Add photo' on screen, but their spoken names are 'Add 10 to stock, <product>', 'Hide <product>' and 'Add a photo of <product>'. A person using voice control who says 'click Hide from app' or 'click +10 stock' gets nothing, because the spoken name does not contain the words they see.
expected: Each spoken name starts with the words shown on the button, then adds the product name.
fix_line: Make each spoken name begin with the button's visible words

title: On a workout offer, member names open the member's page but look like plain text
what: In the list of members in a workout offer, each name is a link to that member's page, but it is drawn in the normal text colour with no underline and no arrow. Nothing tells a first-time user the name can be tapped.
expected: The name looks tappable: link colour or underline, or an arrow at the end of the row.
how_often: every time the offer list is shown
fix_line: Show the member name as a link or add an arrow to the row

title: The colour dots on each product choice are smaller than the panel's own finger-size rule
what: When a product comes in flavours or sizes, each choice row has a row of colour dots to tap. They are 32 dots across, while the panel's own rule for anything tappable is 44. On a phone they sit close together and are easy to miss.
expected: Each colour dot has a tap area of at least 44 by 44, as the bigger colour dots higher in the same form already do.
who: owners editing products on a phone
how_often: every time a choice colour is picked
fix_line: Give the small colour dots the same 44 tap area as the big ones
